summary: Extends the IPFIX flow export protocol and its information model to carry hierarchical structured data and lists of information elements in data records. This allows complex structures such as variable-length lists and containment relationships between templates.

eli5.summary: IPFIX is a way to report on network traffic. This adds the ability to send nested lists, like a shopping list with sub-lists, instead of only flat rows of facts.

questions: what is a subtemplatelist in ipfix
subtitle: How IPFIX can export nested lists of data, not just flat rows of single values.

tldr.problem: IPFIX Data Records are flat lists of single-valued fields, so it cannot express lists of varying length or hierarchies such as MPLS label stacks or multicast output interfaces without awkward workarounds.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC adds three Information Elements and abstract data types, basicList, subTemplateList and subTemplateMultiList, plus a Semantic field and a registry of six semantics that say how the list members relate to each other.
tldr.outcome: Exporters can send variable-length and nested structures in a single Data Record, with Templates referenced from inside the data. Collectors must handle the added decoding complexity, which the RFC flags as a security risk.

today: RFC 6313 is a Proposed Standard from July 2011. It updates RFC 5102 and, per the unit metadata, has not been obsoleted or updated by a later RFC.

sections.title: The Limits of Flat Records
sections.content:
The IPFIX protocol (RFC 5101) exports Flow information using Template Records that define {type, length} pairs and Data Records that carry the values. Its information model (RFC 5102) supports only basic, single-valued data types such as numbers, strings and network addresses. A Data Record is a flat list of single-valued attributes.

The RFC gives concrete pain points. An early NetFlow MPLS design used a position element followed by a value element, which forced element order and needed hard-coded logic in the Collector. The IPFIX model instead defines a long series of elements, mplsTopLabelStackSection and mplsLabelStackSection2 through mplsLabelStackSection10, which clutters the registry and leaves no room for an eleventh next to the others.

Other use cases include the output interfaces of a multicast Flow, BGP AS paths and communities, one-way delay measurements that would otherwise repeat a 5-tuple in every record, and an IPS alert with nested participants, attackers and targets. Flattening the alert would force a unique Template for every alert, wasting CPU, memory and export bandwidth.
sections.eli5: A flat form can hold one answer per line. But some things, like all the rooms a visitor walked through, need a list of any length, and the old form could not hold that.

sections.title: Three New List Types
sections.content:
The RFC defines three abstract data types, each with a matching Information Element that uses the new list data type semantic. Unlike the single-valued types of RFC 5102, they are structural: they mostly contain references to other Information Elements and Templates.

  • basicList: zero or more instances of one Information Element, such as a list of port numbers, interface indexes or ASes in a BGP AS-PATH.
  • subTemplateList: zero or more Data Records that all follow the same single Template Record, such as pairs of MPLS label stack position and value.
  • subTemplateMultiList: zero or more Data Records where different elements can follow different Templates, such as access-list entries built from different criteria.

Because a Template can itself contain a structured data element, these types can describe complex hierarchies. The RFC prefers the term Data Record to Flow Record for this reason. The IANA element IDs are 291 for basicList, 292 for subTemplateList and 293 for subTemplateMultiList.
sections.eli5: There are three kinds of list boxes. One holds many of the same kind of thing. One holds many copies of the same little form. The third holds little forms of different kinds.

sections.title: Encoding the Lists
sections.content:
All new elements MUST be sent in network byte order. Each starts with a one-octet Semantic field. A basicList then carries a Field ID (with an Enterprise bit, and a four-byte Enterprise Number if that bit is 1), a 16-bit Element Length and the content. The Element Length is part of the header, so even a zero-element list MUST NOT omit it. A subTemplateList carries a Template ID followed by zero or more Data Records. A subTemplateMultiList repeats a Template ID, a Data Records Length and the records for each Template.

The Collecting Process decodes content until no data remains, so no count is sent. Decoding is recursive if a referenced Template holds more structured data.

When length varies, the RFC recommends the variable-length encoding from RFC 5101, using the three-byte form (the value 255 followed by a 16-bit length) even for lengths under 255, because the Exporter can write the final length after encoding. Exporters MUST NOT exceed the maximum IPFIX message length of 65535 bytes.
sections.eli5: Each list box has a label on the front saying how the items relate, and what kind of items they are. The reader keeps unpacking until the box is empty.

sections.title: Semantics of a List
sections.content:
The Semantic field tells the Collector how the list members relate to the Data Record. There are six values in a new IANA subregistry.

  • undefined (the default): no semantic given, so the Collector draws its own conclusions.
  • noneOf: none of the elements are actual properties of the record, for example attack types a mediator already ruled out.
  • exactlyOneOf: exactly one element applies (a logical XOR), for example one egress interface chosen by load balancing.
  • oneOrMoreOf: one or more apply (a logical OR).
  • allOf: all apply, as for a multicast Flow replicated to every listed interface.
  • ordered: the elements are ordered, as in the BGP AS-PATH AS10 AS20 AS30 AS40.

Semantics can be combined. The RFC shows a path with an ordered part and an exactlyOneOf part, AS50, AS60, as a basicList of two basicLists. A single-element list SHOULD use the default undefined semantic.
sections.eli5: The label also says what the list means: none of these, only one of these, any of these, all of these, or these in order.

sections.title: Choosing a Representation and Managing Templates
sections.content:
The same data can often be written more than one way. A basicList is RECOMMENDED over a subTemplateList that holds a single element, because it needs no extra Template. A subTemplateList is RECOMMENDED over a one-element subTemplateMultiList, because it tells the Collector the element types are consistent. The top-level semantic of a subTemplateMultiList cannot describe relations within one Template's records, so for cases such as attacker A1 or A2 attacking targets T1 and T2 the RFC shows a basicList of subTemplateLists.

Template ID uniqueness is unchanged from RFC 5101: it is local to the Transport Session and Observation Domain. A Template no longer in use SHOULD be deleted with a Template Withdrawal Message, a deleted Template MUST NOT be used in a list, and it MUST be deleted before its ID is reused.

Structured Data Information Elements MAY appear in Options Template Sets, including as scope. A Collector that does not support the extension can ignore these elements or the records that contain them.
sections.eli5: If you can do the job with a simple box, use the simple box. And when you throw away an old form, say so before you reuse its number.

sections.title: Worked Examples and Related Specs
sections.content:
Section 9 of the RFC shows byte-level encodings. They include a multicast record with a basicList of egress interfaces 1, 4, 8 under Template ID 256, a subTemplateList, a subTemplateMultiList, an Options Template using structured data, and an IPS alert hierarchy. The RFC states the examples are only illustrations of the encoding.

The RFC also relates structured data to other IPFIX work. It can replace the Common Properties technique of RFC 5473 in simple cases, with a single Template for the Collector to manage, although the RFC notes a detailed analysis of the bandwidth gain was not done. Because PSAMP builds on IPFIX, the specification applies to PSAMP too, and it helps mediation functions export aggregated records.
sections.eli5: The document includes sample filled-in forms, so implementers can check their own work against them.

sections.title: IANA Registrations
sections.content:
The RFC adds the three abstract data types to the IPFIX Information Element Data Types registry, adds list to the data type semantics, and registers the three Information Elements. It creates the "IPFIX Structured Data Types Semantics" subregistry, an 8-bit value space where new entries need a Standards Action.

The initial values are 0xFF for undefined, 0x00 for noneOf, 0x01 for exactlyOneOf, 0x02 for oneOrMoreOf, 0x03 for allOf and 0x04 for ordered.
sections.eli5: The official number list now has entries for the new box types and for each meaning label.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The RFC warns that complex data types complicate Collector implementations, which could easily lead to new vulnerabilities such as buffer overflows. The risk is higher when DTLS is not used, or when the Observation Point and Collector are in different trust domains. Otherwise the security considerations of RFC 5101 and RFC 5102 apply.
sections.eli5: Opening boxes inside boxes is trickier, and a sneaky sender could try to confuse a careless reader, so readers must be careful.

fields.name: E
fields.desc: Enterprise bit; 1 adds a four-byte Enterprise Number after the Element Length.

fields.name: Field ID
fields.desc: Information Element identifier of the list elements.

fields.name: Element Length
fields.desc: Length of each element, or 0xFFFF if variable-length encoded.

fields.name: Template ID
fields.desc: Template used to decode the content.

items.label: noneOf
items.desc: None of the elements are properties of the record.

items.label: oneOrMoreOf
items.desc: One or more elements apply (logical OR).

cells: Data Records of a single Template
